newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton loses ground on sluggish mill buying.
newsitem.headline: India cotton loses ground on sluggish mill buying.

text.p: Indian cotton prices lost ground on sluggish mill buying and higher new crop expectations that prompted fresh selling on Wednesday, dealers said.
In the spot deals Punjab saw-ginned slid by 20/30 rupees at 1,820/1,855 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi fell by 10 rupees at 1,050/1,090 rupees per maund.
"The cotton market was firm on Tuesday following price hikes announced by state-owned agencies but sluggish mill buying again dragged prices lower," one broker said.
"Spinning mills face rising stockpiles of cotton yarn due to lower than expected overseas buying which in turn has curtailed offtake of cotton by these mills," he said.

In the Gujarat segment, Kalyan cotton dropped by 300 rupees at 14,200/14,700 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while Wagad cotton moved down by 100 rupees at 13,000/13,200 rupees and Kala-ginned fell by 100 rupees at 12,300/12,400 rupees per candy.
